candidate.title: Nanogrid / SNRS
candidate.scope: The central Nanogrid / SNRS row of the assigned Illumina schematic: nanogrid single-nucleus RNA sequencing, with the explicitly depicted single-cell input alternative, from stained suspension and pre-existing oligo-lined wells through image-guided well selection, lysis, poly(A) capture and barcoded cDNA library generation. Nanogrid is the platform-qualified name in this row and SNRS is its single-nucleus RNA-seq abbreviation, not evidence that every nanogrid assay has this architecture. The upper Microwell-Seq captions, lower MULTI-Seq row and right-hand biotin legend are neighboring context, not additional target workflows or reagents for this row. The polyA RNA icon is the biological target, not an upstream bulk RNA-extraction step. No experimental recipe or complete paper workflow is reconstructed.

states.label: Stained single-cell or nuclear suspension
features: Alternative biological inputs share the depicted nanogrid route; the polyA RNA icon identifies the RNA target inside the cell or nucleus, rather than an extracted RNA input.
The drawing explicitly labels DAPI-stained nuclei. The paper distinguishes DAPI-stained nuclei from PI/Hoechst-stained whole cells.

states.label: Barcoded cDNA library flanked by sequencing adapters
features: DNA copies of captured polyadenylated RNA are the sequenced carrier; the source target is RNA from selected cells or nuclei.

The paper identifies a 3′ RNA-sequencing readout; this does not establish full-length transcript reconstruction or equal coverage of all RNA species.

operations.label: Dispense
operations.description: Load the stained suspension into the pre-existing oligo-lined nanogrid wells. The output changes the cell/nucleus compartment from suspension to individual nanowells with variable occupancy.
operations.mechanism: A nanodispenser places cells or nuclei into nanowells.
operations.information_effect: Establishes a spatial well address that can later be associated with a preprinted well barcode; it does not yet attach that barcode to a transcript.

operations.label: Fluorescent microscopy imaging
operations.description: Inspect occupied and unoccupied wells, producing fluorescence/occupancy information while leaving cells or nuclei in their wells. The cell and nucleus examples are alternative inputs to the same depicted inspection.
operations.mechanism: Fluorescence distinguishes single occupancy from none/dead or multiple occupancy. Paper resolves cellular live/dead screening versus selection of intact DAPI-positive nuclei.
operations.information_effect: Provides a well-associated selection record. Imaging reduces unwanted occupancy and dead-cell inclusion but does not guarantee zero doublets or perfect sample purity.

operations.label: Select viable wells & lyse
operations.description: Use well-associated image information to choose wells containing one accepted cell or nucleus, then lyse selected contents to expose RNA. The unselected empty/dead or multiple-occupancy wells remain outside the library route.
operations.mechanism: The paper specifies reagent deposition only into selected wells. Its nuclear criterion is intact DAPI-positive nuclei, rather than viability of isolated nuclei.
operations.information_effect: Retains selected well identity and excludes the other well categories from the intended library. The diagram’s word sorted denotes selection by imaging, not an evidenced physical transfer of intact cells into a new compartment.

operations.label: cDNA library generation — RT, template switching and one-sided P7 tagmentation
operations.description: Convert captured RNA into barcoded cDNA and generate adapter-flanked library molecules. Within this broad depicted block, the primary paper places mixing after per-well RT: barcoded cDNA is pooled for subsequent library preparation. Pooling is retained as this block’s compartment transition, without adding an independently drawn pooling operation.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription creates DNA copies using well-associated barcode/UMI/P5-containing primers; template switching supplies a second adapter for cDNA synthesis/enrichment. The paper reports pooling after RT, and the diagram labels the subsequent library interface as one-sided P7 tagmentation.
operations.information_effect: The cDNA carrier retains transcript-derived sequence, well barcode and designed UMI, preserving the well-to-source association when cDNA compartments are mixed. The paper reports pooled libraries demultiplexed by well barcode; transcript-derived reads can therefore be assigned to the selected cells/nuclei to summarize 3′ expression profiles. The depicted UMI supports molecular identification in the library design; no absolute counting accuracy is established here.

The graph retains loading, inspection, selected/unselected outcomes, capture and library generation at the diagram’s resolution. Joint operations represent loading into wells, imaging with a data output, and image-guided selection, rather than merging independent molecular branches. No consequential unsupported claim, missing depicted transformation, incompatible interface or unresolved paper association remains at the declared schematic scope.
